elements.element: Workers' compensation as required by law
elements.evidence: "workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law"
"provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request"
"errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000" exceeds USD 1M floor
"cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" exceeds USD 2M floor

reasons: All six preferred elements are expressly present at the stated limits, party direction (Kubient as insurer, Customer as recipient of certificates) and the request-based certificate mechanic are correct.

The insertion is an appropriate concise addition because no insurance clause existed anywhere in the Agreement; existing Section 14(i) text is untouched and no undefined term is introduced ('Term' and 'Law' are Agreement-defined).

Minimality is marginally exceeded: the preferred position asks only for the listed coverages and certificates, not a one-year post-termination coverage tail ('and for one (1) year thereafter'), which adds protection beyond the selected level. This is a low-impact drafting excess in our favour, not a substantive defect.
